attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 9.5 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (read-only standbys) on Ubuntu 16.04. Installed postgresql/postgresql-contrib on all three nodes, created a replicator role on node1, configured wal_level/max_wal_senders/wal_keep_segments/hot_standby and pg_hba.conf for replication, took pg_basebackup snapshots to seed node2/node3, and configured recovery.conf in standby_mode on both. Verified data written on the primary (repl_test table) replicates to both standbys and that standbys reject writes (read-only). Then performed the mandatory sequential node-restart protocol (node2, node3, node1) using `shutdown -r now` backgrounded so acks returned before disconnection; confirmed each node's boot_id changed post-restart, confirmed PostgreSQL auto-started and standbys resumed streaming replication and retained data across restarts, and confirmed a post-primary-restart write again propagated to both standbys.
